acceptanceCriteria: Measure btime stability on a GitHub Linux runner and record the result.
Either keep btime with a tolerance or migrate identities to a stable boot identifier, with an explicit compatibility decision for persisted ledgers, markers and run records.
A test proves a live process keeps a matching identity when btime differs by one second.
body: Suspected defect found 2026-10-10 while diagnosing the PR #725 dispatch flake (branch claude/dispatch-detached-rig-flake, commit 0c77b817). Linux process identities are linux:<btime>:<starttime> (internal/tasks/supervisor/identity_linux.go). In a docker golang:1.27.1 VM, 3000 samples of /proc/stat btime gave 1789760570 1076 times and 1789760571 1924 times, so a live process's identity can stop matching its recorded one. Under stress this produced: DeferralIsBounded 'released [claim]' after endWorker; SupervisorLostHandsOffWithoutRelaunch handing off without a SUPERVISOR_LOST alert; and an index-out-of-range panic in newDetachedRig (leader identity mismatched, empty tree, worker accounted ended while running). Production consequence: a running worker can be treated as ended/ORPHANED and a detached supervisor can fail verification. internal/tasks/service/descendants_linux.go:248 and internal/postmergeproof/procfs/procfs_linux.go:25 already use /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id. Fixing changes a persisted identity format (ledger, markers, run records), so it needs a migration decision. Frequency on GitHub runners: NOT_OBSERVED. Expected: identity of a live process is stable across reads. Actual: it can flip with btime rounding.

holds.reason: Owner decision: persisted process identity (+/-1 s tolerance or boot_id migration), plus a Linux-runner measurement.

title: Suspected: Linux process identity uses /proc/stat btime, which jitters by one second between reads
